title: County Line Pews
concept_summary: Musically, it lives in americana / heartland-adjacent with southern-gospel shadow and stays with blue-collar man used to practical fixes; uneasy in church with belief still catching; older-brother figure carrying what he kept quiet; morally trapped by what he cannot fix. The pressure comes from ritual pressure on a practical man carrying what he kept quiet. It leaves the release in silence, non-participation, and what he still does not say.

signal_stack.identity: blue-collar man used to practical fixes; uneasy in church with belief still catching; older-brother figure carrying what he kept quiet; morally trapped by what he cannot fix
signal_stack.emotional_arc: Belief residue -> ritual discomfort -> withheld confession
signal_stack.production_layer: steady guitar bed, held-in lead vocal, low harmony shadow

lyrics:
[Intro]
folded bulletin in his fist
hymn he can't quite sing

[Verse 1]
mud still dried on work boots
kept his mouth shut when it counted most
hands that know a wrench ain't good for this

[Pre-Chorus]
county line / two-lane / ditch water / sheriff lights way back in memory
room gets quiet and it all comes back
lets it pass when it gets to him

[Chorus]
communion tray comin' closer
he lets it pass
that hymn stays caught halfway back

[Bridge]
could tell it plain, still don't
tray gets to his row, he keeps his hands down

[Outro]
folded bulletin in his fist
tray goes by and he don't move
